result.summary: Adds C++20 consteval compile-time verification for RPC argument names and result field names. The checks reject confusing or non-standard name formats during compilation to enforce naming consistency. It also disables the modernize-use-emplace clang-tidy check where it conflicts with consteval name evaluation.
result.problem: Inconsistently or improperly formatted RPC argument and field names can create user confusion and bugs across RPC interfaces. Developers currently lack automated compile-time enforcement against invalid or confusing naming patterns when registering RPC endpoints.
evidence: PR description notes that non-snake_case names lead to "bugs and confusion" citing PR #35317.
result.scope_notes: The diff was not provided, but commit messages indicate changes across RPC definition machinery and clang-tidy configuration.
result.card: Adds C++20 consteval compile-time checks to validate RPC argument names and result field names during build. This solves the problem of inconsistently named RPC parameters and result fields leading to bugs and developer confusion, as noted in PR #35317. It also adjusts clang-tidy configuration to disable modernize-use-emplace where it interferes with consteval names.
uncertainties: Exact naming pattern rules and touched RPC files cannot be verified because the diff is not available.

risk.why: A mistake in compile-time naming validation would fail the build for developers rather than introducing runtime regressions or consensus issues.
